uc-ai-reporting-launch.title: Launch AI Reporting
uc-ai-reporting-launch.what: Full path from "we have manual reports" to "working weekly report workflow". Path through 6 105 Atlas nodes: Foundation, then [[node:ai-fundamentals|AI Fundamentals]], then Configuration, then Transformation.
uc-ai-reporting-launch.why: This is the most common ops-team request: "AI can write reports, how do we start?". A Use Case gives a clear route instead of "start reading everything".
uc-ai-reporting-launch.when: When there is a regular report (weekly/monthly) taking ≥3 hours per week. When data is available (CRM/analytics with export). When there is team buy-in.
uc-ai-reporting-launch.impact: Outcome: working weekly report workflow in 2 weeks of work. Metrics: time-to-report from 4h to 30min, consistency +90%, team buy-in measurable (NPS survey).
uc-ai-reporting-launch.example:
Path (6 steps through nodes):
1. Foundation: prompting, then how to write a [[node:b-system|system prompt]] for a report
2. Foundation: af-rag-basics, then if the report needs CRM context, how to feed it to Claude
3. Foundation: projects, then create a "Weekly Reports" workspace for the team
4. Foundation: i-claudemd, then describe the report format in [[node:cc-md|CLAUDE.md]]
5. Transformation: ops-reporting-automation, then concrete workflow with stages
6. Transformation: sc-data, then how to work with CSV data

Day 1-3: Setup Project + write first prompt manually.
Day 4-7: Iterate on 5-10 real reports.
Day 8-14: Roll-out to the team + feedback.

Stage transition: from stage 1 to stage 2.
uc-ai-reporting-launch.mistakes: Wanting "full automation" in the first week. First AI writes a draft, then human edits, then measure quality. Only after 5-10 successful iterations — add automation (triggers, scheduling).

uc-ai-process-automation.title: Automate a Recurring Process
uc-ai-process-automation.what: Path to automating a specific operations process via AI. From candidate identification to a production-ready workflow with Skills + Hooks.
uc-ai-process-automation.why: Operations teams often get stuck at "we tried Claude, liked it" — but do not know how to make it systematic. This UC shows a structured approach.
uc-ai-process-automation.when: When there is a process running ≥5×/week with clear inputs/outputs. When result variability is a problem. When there is technical capability for triggers/integrations.
uc-ai-process-automation.impact: Outcome: automated workflow with quality gates in 2-3 weeks. Metrics: time savings 70-90%, error rate <5%, team satisfaction +.
uc-ai-process-automation.example:
Path (6 steps):
1. Identification: pick the process — this is ops-process-automation
2. Foundation: skills + s-create, then build a reusable Skill
3. Foundation: mcp, then if external integrations are needed
4. Foundation: cc-hooks, then automatic triggers
5. Foundation: prompting, then core workflow prompt
6. Transformation: ops-process-automation, then structure with quality gates

Week 1: Document the process as-is. Identify AI-replaceable steps.
Week 2: Build the Skill + first tests on historical data.
Week 3: Production roll-out with monitoring.

Stage transition: from stage 1 to stage 2 (if first automation) or from stage 2 to stage 3 (expansion).
uc-ai-process-automation.mistakes: Automating without stabilizing the process. If the process is still changing — the workflow will constantly break. And: not making quality gates. Without human review = automated trash.

uc-ai-decision-support.title: AI Support for Operational Decisions
uc-ai-decision-support.what: Rolling out AI structuring for operational decisions in the team. From ad-hoc "let us discuss in Slack" to a structured decision process with AI analysis.
uc-ai-decision-support.why: Operations teams make 5-10 decisions a week under load. Without structure — lots of reactive, little learning. AI adds discipline without bureaucracy.
uc-ai-decision-support.when: When decisions require trade-off analysis (hire vs no-hire, vendor selection, process change). When retrospective shows "we decided this a year ago and forgot".
uc-ai-decision-support.impact: Outcome: working decision process with AI support in 3-4 weeks. Metrics: reactive decisions ↓50-70%, learning loop established (retrospective with AI pattern matching).
uc-ai-decision-support.example:
Path (6 steps):
1. Identification: which decisions to include (Operations: hires, vendors, processes)
2. Foundation: prompting + pr-cot (chain-of-thought) — structure of AI analysis
3. Foundation: sc-data + sc-analysis, then how to feed data for the decision
4. Foundation: af-llm-basics, then understand AI boundaries: where it gives value, where it errs
5. Foundation: projects, then "Decision Log" workspace with history
6. Transformation: ops-decision-intelligence, then concrete workflow

Week 1: Pilot on 3-5 simple decisions.
Week 2-3: Refine template + verify quality.
Week 4: Roll-out to all major decisions + retrospective.

Stage transition: from stage 2 to stage 3.
uc-ai-decision-support.mistakes: Using AI as "the decider". AI is good at structuring and pattern matching, but context and accountability belong to the human. Documentation matters more than the AI output itself: track outcomes, then learn, then improve.

mk-content-ops.title: AI Content Operations
mk-content-ops.what: Content machine on AI: input (brief), then AI draft, then human review, then publish. Pipeline for blog posts, email, social, documentation. Goal — 10× speedup without losing brand voice.
mk-content-ops.why: Content teams spend 40-60% of time on drafts. AI handles 80% of this work. Freed time goes to strategy, distribution, performance analysis — where AI does not help.
mk-content-ops.when: When the team publishes ≥10 pieces per month. When there is a documented brand voice (or it is easy to assemble). When SEO/audience research exists as brief input.
mk-content-ops.impact: Time-to-publish: from 2 days to 4 hours. Content output: +200-300% with the same team. Consistency: single tone across all channels.
mk-content-ops.example:
Content Pipeline:

  Brief (topic + outline + audience)
        ↓
  Project "Blog" with brand voice prompt
        ↓
  AI draft (800 words in 2 minutes)
        ↓
  Quality gate: editor review
        ↓
  Final + SEO optimization
        ↓
  Publish

Metric: 1500-word longread in 4 hours instead of 2 days.
mk-content-ops.mistakes: Doing "AI generates, then publish" without a human gate. Any AI text needs review: factcheck, tone, local context. Without human-in-the-loop — generic AI content the reader spots in 3 seconds.

mk-campaign-intel.title: AI Campaign Intelligence
mk-campaign-intel.what: AI support for planning and analyzing marketing campaigns: performance prediction, creative variant generation, post-mortem analysis. AI = "second analyst" on the team.
mk-campaign-intel.why: Campaigns are planned under pressure, then reactive decisions, no learning loop. AI adds structured analysis pre-launch (what to try) and post-launch (what worked and why).
mk-campaign-intel.when: Quarterly campaign planning. Before launching a campaign with >$10k budget. Post-mortem after every major campaign. A/B testing copy.
mk-campaign-intel.impact: Campaign ROI: +20-40% thanks to better planning and faster learning. Reduce reactive decisions: 60%.
mk-campaign-intel.example:
Campaign workflow:

  Pre-launch:
  1. AI analyzes past campaigns to similar audience
  2. Generates 5 angle/positioning variants
  3. Predicts likely performance (rough)

  Post-launch:
  1. AI reads all metrics + comments
  2. Pattern-matching: what worked, what did not
  3. Documents learnings in shared knowledge base

After a year: organized library of campaign learnings.
mk-campaign-intel.mistakes: Using AI as "ROI predictor". AI is good at pattern matching historical data, but new markets/channels are beyond its experience. AI = "thoughtful colleague for brainstorming", not "oracle".

mk-brand-voice.title: AI Brand Voice Tuning
mk-brand-voice.what: Documenting and codifying brand voice in the AI generation system. From ad-hoc "we need to sound like us" — to explicit voice guide + system prompts + [[node:pr-fewshot|few-shot examples]] in every Project.
mk-brand-voice.why: Without explicit voice, AI outputs generic "like everyone". With voice guide — text sounds like your team. This is the difference between "AI is noticeable" and "AI is invisible".
mk-brand-voice.when: When team ≥3 people writes content. When "AI tone is not us" complaints. Before AI content operations roll-out to the whole team. When brand vocabulary matters (B2B, tech, lifestyle).
mk-brand-voice.impact: Brand consistency: from 60% to 95%. Editor rewrite time: -70%. New team member onboarding: -50%.
mk-brand-voice.example:
Brand Voice Setup:

1. "Voice Guide" document:
   - 3-5 voice attributes (e.g., warm, expert, direct)
   - Do/Don't examples for each
   - 10 sample paragraphs in our style

2. [[node:b-system|System prompt]] in "Blog" Project:
   "You write in style X. Voice attributes: ... Examples: ..."

3. Test: 5 different people give brief, then AI generates, then blind review, then > 80% pick AI-version vs generic.

Real investment: 2-3 days for setup, saves hours per piece.
mk-brand-voice.mistakes: Describing voice abstractly ("professional but friendly"). It does not help AI. Voice = examples + concrete attributes + Do/Don't. More concrete, better reproducibility.

mk-seo-optimization.title: AI SEO at Scale
mk-seo-optimization.what: AI for SEO tasks: keyword research, content briefs from SERPs, meta optimization, internal linking. From 1 SEO specialist per 5 content writers — to a team where every writer is SEO-aware.
mk-seo-optimization.why: SEO requires expertise content writers usually do not have. AI closes the gap: author writes, AI checks/suggests SEO improvements. Team moves faster without hiring an SEO spec.
mk-seo-optimization.when: When content output >20 pieces/month + SEO is critical (B2B SaaS, eCommerce, content-driven). When there is budget for keyword research tools (ahrefs/semrush).
mk-seo-optimization.impact: Organic traffic: +30-60% in 6 months. SEO coverage rate (% of pages targeting keywords): from 30% to 80%.
mk-seo-optimization.example:
SEO Workflow:

  1. Author writes draft on topic.
  2. AI Step: "here are top-10 SERPs for this topic, then what competitors cover, what is missing"
  3. AI Step: "based on this draft + SERP gap analysis, what subtopics to add, what keywords to integrate"
  4. Author redrafts with AI recommendations.
  5. AI Step: meta title + description optimization.

Result: SEO-optimized content without a separate SEO pass.
mk-seo-optimization.mistakes: Trusting AI keyword research fully. AI does not know current trends (cutoff date) and does not see fresh SERPs. Use AI as "SEO advisor", but keyword data — from specialized tools.

mk-performance-analytics.title: AI Marketing Performance Analytics
mk-performance-analytics.what: AI reads marketing metrics (GA, social, email), then writes insight-driven reports with hypotheses and action items. From "here are graphs, figure it out" — to "here is what happened and what we do".
mk-performance-analytics.why: Marketing teams drown in dashboards without actionable insights. AI does the narrative layer: connects dots, explains anomalies, suggests hypotheses. Decision velocity grows.
mk-performance-analytics.when: Weekly/monthly performance reviews. When the team spends >2 hours per week collecting reports. When the "reason" for metric drops is non-obvious.
mk-performance-analytics.impact: Time-to-insight: from days to hours. Quality of weekly reviews: structured insights instead of "here are numbers".
mk-performance-analytics.example:
Weekly Marketing Performance Report:

  Inputs:
  - GA4 export (traffic, conversions)
  - Email metrics (open rate, CTR)
  - Social engagement
  - Campaign spend

  AI Output:
  - What grew/dropped (numbers + delta)
  - Hypotheses why (based on past patterns)
  - 3 recommendations for next week
  - Red flags (what needs deeper investigation)

  Human: 15 min validation + 3 decomposed actions.
mk-performance-analytics.mistakes: Using AI as an "attribution engine". AI does not know the real attribution model (multi-touch, view-through). Use AI for narrative and pattern matching, not for exact causation.

mk-team-workflow.title: AI Marketing Team Workflow
mk-team-workflow.what: How a marketing team orchestrates working with AI: shared brand voice, content templates, weekly AI office hours, knowledge sharing. From "everyone with their own Claude" — to a collaborative AI system.
mk-team-workflow.why: Individual usage in marketing does not scale — voice is not consistent, templates duplicate, learnings are lost. Team workflow = single standard + shared library + faster onboarding.
mk-team-workflow.when: Marketing team ≥3 people actively use AI. Inconsistent results emerge. New team members "do not know how we work with AI".
mk-team-workflow.impact: Team velocity: +30-50%. New writer time-to-productive: from 2 weeks to 3-5 days. Knowledge retention: shared Projects + voice guide = team learns from common mistakes.
mk-team-workflow.example:
Marketing Team Setup:

1. Shared Claude Project "Marketing Workspace"
2. Files: brand voice guide, content templates, SEO playbook
3. [[node:cc-md|CLAUDE.md]]: "content rules + naming conventions"
4. Reusable Skills: blog-post-writer, email-drafter, social-snippet
5. Weekly "AI office hours" 30 min: team shows winning prompts, discusses fails
6. Metric: % of content done via shared workflow vs ad-hoc

Stage 3 sign: new writer is productive in 3-5 days, everyone has consistent quality.
mk-team-workflow.mistakes: Making "team workflow" = "one person dictates". Team workflow = collaboration. Each contributor, then updates workflow + ownership over one part (voice guide, templates, SEO). Shared ownership = sustainable system.

uc-ai-content-ops-launch.title: Launch AI Content Operations
uc-ai-content-ops-launch.what: Full path from "we have generic AI texts" to "working content machine with brand voice". Cross-layer path through 7 nodes: Foundation, then Configuration, then Systems, then Transformation.
uc-ai-content-ops-launch.why: The most common marketing-team request: "AI writes but does not sound like us". This UC solves the problem systematically — through explicit brand voice setup + content pipeline.
uc-ai-content-ops-launch.when: When the team already uses AI ad-hoc but quality is inconsistent. When output >10 pieces/month. When there is buy-in from editor/content lead.
uc-ai-content-ops-launch.impact: Outcome: working content pipeline with brand voice in 2 weeks. Metrics: time-to-publish from 2 days to 4h, brand consistency from 60% to 90%, content output +200%.

Path (7 steps):

1. Foundation: prompting, then how to formulate briefs for AI
2. Foundation: b-system, then how to write a [[node:b-system|system prompt]] with voice
3. Foundation: i-style + instructions, then [[node:instructions|custom instructions]] at profile level

cs-tier1.title: AI Tier-1 Automation
cs-tier1.what: Automating first-line support: AI reads incoming ticket, then finds answer in knowledge base (RAG), then writes a personalized reply, or escalates to a human. Pipeline with explicit quality gates.
cs-tier1.why: 30-50% of all support tickets are repeat questions (password reset, billing, account access). AI closes this mass with consistent quality. Tier-2 agents focus on complex.
cs-tier1.when: Tier-1 volume >100 tickets/week. Structured knowledge base. Clear FAQ categories (40%+ tickets fit into 20 patterns). Buy-in from CS-lead.
cs-tier1.impact: Deflection: 40-60%. Median response time: from 4h to 2min for AI-tickets. Tier-2 load drops by 30-40%. CSAT for AI-tickets: 4.2/5 with right setup (vs 4.4 for humans).
cs-tier1.example:
Tier-1 Workflow:

  Incoming ticket
        ↓
  [Classify intent: FAQ vs complex]
   ├─ FAQ leads to AI processes with KB
   │         ↓
   │     [Confidence > 0.8?]
   │      ├─ Yes leads to AI response + log
   │      └─ No  leads to escalate to tier-2 with AI summary
   └─ Complex leads to directly to human queue

  Quality gate: 10% random AI responses, then human review weekly

Metric: deflection rate weekly, CSAT for AI-tickets.
cs-tier1.mistakes: Doing tier-1 at 80% content. Edge cases accumulate: every AI failure = bad experience. Production rule: AI responds only when confidence is high. Otherwise escalate with AI-prepared context for the human.

cs-agent-assist.title: AI Agent Assist
cs-agent-assist.what: AI as a "co-pilot" for tier-2 agent: real-time response suggestions, autocompletion, similar-case search, template generation. Agent stays in the driver seat, AI accelerates.
cs-agent-assist.why: Agent-assist is less risky than tier-1: human is always in the loop. ROI is faster (response time -50% immediately). Team sees AI as "helper", not "threat". Adoption is much higher.
cs-agent-assist.when: Tier-2/3 team spends time writing responses from scratch. There are historical tickets with good answers. Want to raise velocity without quality loss.
cs-agent-assist.impact: Response time per ticket: from 8 min to 3 min. Agents handle 50-70% more tickets/day. Quality consistent (AI used as draft, agent edits). New agent onboarding: -50% (AI compensates junior gap).
cs-agent-assist.example:
Agent Assist Setup:

1. Browser plugin or helpdesk integration.
2. Open ticket, then AI reads context + customer history.
3. AI suggests:
   - 3 reply variants (formal/friendly/technical)
   - Similar past tickets (resolved)
   - Relevant KB articles
4. Agent selects + edits + sends.
5. AI learns from agent edits (improves suggestions over time).

Real usage: 70% suggestions accepted with minor edits, 20% edited significantly, 10% unused.
cs-agent-assist.mistakes: Forcing agents to use AI "mandatorily". If a suggestion is bad — it forces writing from scratch. Drive adoption through value (show time saved per ticket), not mandate.

cs-knowledge-base.title: AI Knowledge Base Operations
cs-knowledge-base.what: Knowledge base turns from "PDF dump" into a living AI system: vector search, auto-updates based on resolved tickets, gap analysis (what is often asked but no article exists), structured taxonomy.
cs-knowledge-base.why: Without a good KB, all AI support fails. KB = single source of truth for AI. KB quality ≠ article count. Quality KB ops = more impact than just launching AI.
cs-knowledge-base.when: In parallel with tier-1 setup. When AI bot answers "I do not know" to >20% of questions. When agents complain "cannot find the article". When KB has not been updated in >6 months.
cs-knowledge-base.impact: KB findability: from 50% to 90% (vector search vs keyword). AI deflection rate grows +15-20% (more coverage). Agent onboarding: -40% time.
cs-knowledge-base.example:
KB Ops Pipeline:

Weekly:
  1. AI reads resolved tickets for the week.
  2. Identifies frequent questions without KB articles.
  3. Drafts new KB articles from ticket solutions.
  4. KB editor reviews + publishes.

Monthly:
  1. AI analyzes KB usage (which articles cited).
  2. Flags outdated content (product changed, article did not).
  3. Suggests merges (duplicate articles).

Metric: % of tickets where AI found KB match, up over time.
cs-knowledge-base.mistakes: Making KB only for humans. Modern KB optimization = for AI + humans. Structure (clear headers, atomic articles, metadata) matters for AI retrieval. Otherwise AI does not find — even if the article exists.

cs-escalation.title: AI Escalation Intelligence
cs-escalation.what: Smart escalation: AI decides when to hand off to a human and exactly to whom (by specialization, load, severity). Plus prepares escalation context — the agent gets not "here is a ticket", but "here is a ticket + history + what AI tried".
cs-escalation.why: Dumb escalation = ticket arrives without context, agent spends 5 minutes reading. Smart = agent sees summary + what was already tried + recommended next step. Velocity grows without quality loss.
cs-escalation.when: When tier-1 AI is running and tier-2 routing is needed. When there are specializations (billing vs technical vs account). When escalation is a bottleneck.
cs-escalation.impact: Time-to-resolution for escalated tickets: -40%. Routing accuracy: from 80% to 95% (correct specialist on first try). Agent satisfaction +: less "why did they pass this to me".
cs-escalation.example:
Escalation Workflow:

  AI cannot resolve ticket
        ↓
  [Classify problem domain]
   ├─ Billing, queue: billing_team
   ├─ Technical, queue: tech_support
   └─ Account, queue: account_specialists
        ↓
  AI prepares escalation summary:
   - Customer info + history
   - What customer wants
   - What AI tried (and why it didn't work)
   - Suggested next step
        ↓
  Agent picks up: context ready in 30 sec instead of 5 min.

Metric: agent feedback on escalation quality.
cs-escalation.mistakes: Escalating "just in case" at low confidence. If AI errs 10% but escalates 50% — it is degradation. Calibrate threshold: too high = killed deflection, too low = bad quality.

cs-quality-monitoring.title: AI Quality Monitoring
cs-quality-monitoring.what: Continuous monitoring of AI response quality: weekly sample, then human review, then identify failure patterns, then adjust prompts/KB. Without monitoring, AI degrades silently: errors accumulate, no one sees.
cs-quality-monitoring.why: AI is not static: KB changes, product changes, customer questions change. AI that worked in Q1 may slip in Q3. Quality monitoring catches drift before CSAT drops.
cs-quality-monitoring.when: From day 1 of AI tier-1 launch. Mandatory. Not "when there is a problem" — continuous. Minimum: 10% AI responses random sample, then weekly review.
cs-quality-monitoring.impact: AI drift detection: before customers notice (CSAT does not drop). Continuous improvement: every week prompts/KB get better. Trust in the AI system grows through explicit quality data.
cs-quality-monitoring.example:
Quality Monitoring Process:

Weekly:
  1. Random sample 10% of AI responses.
  2. Quality team rates: accuracy, tone, completeness.
  3. Failure patterns extracted: "AI confuses billing X with Y", "misses context Z".
  4. Action: update KB articles OR adjust [[node:b-system|system prompt]] OR add edge case to training data.

Metric:
  - % AI responses rated >4/5
  - Trending direction (better/worse week-over-week)
  - Top 3 failure categories

Escalation: if quality < 4/5 for 2 weeks, pause AI tier-1, investigate.
cs-quality-monitoring.mistakes: Monitoring without action loop. If found errors do not lead to changes — it is theater. Quality monitoring must be embedded in weekly product process (Mon: review, Tue: fix, Wed: validate, ...).

cs-support-analytics.title: AI Support Analytics
cs-support-analytics.what: AI reads support metrics + ticket content, then writes insight reports: trending issues, customer sentiment, agent performance patterns, product feedback. Turns support data into product insights.
cs-support-analytics.why: Support is free user research. Thousands of conversations with real customers. But the team drowns in objects/dashboards. AI does the narrative layer + connects to product/marketing teams.
cs-support-analytics.when: Weekly support reviews. When product team wants "voice of customer". When there is a pattern "many complaints about feature X" — need systematic detection.
cs-support-analytics.impact: Time-to-insight: from days to hours. Product team gets trending issues automatically. Customer voice loop closes: from ticket, then insight, then product change, then fewer tickets.
cs-support-analytics.example:
Weekly Support Analytics Report:

  Inputs:
  - All tickets for the week (resolved + open)
  - CSAT scores + comments
  - Agent performance metrics
  - Product release notes

  AI Output:
  - Top 5 trending issues (with ticket count + delta)
  - Sentiment analysis: where customers are frustrated
  - Correlation: "new feature X released, tickets about X +40%"
  - Recommendations for product team
  - Recommendations for KB updates

Distribution: report shared with product + marketing, closing the loop.
cs-support-analytics.mistakes: Doing support analytics in isolation. If insights do not reach product/engineering — they are useless. Set up explicit channels: weekly "Support Insights" Slack post in #product, monthly review session.

cs-team-workflow.title: AI Customer Support Team Workflow
cs-team-workflow.what: CS team operating model with AI: shared knowledge base ops, common agent-assist setup, AI office hours, quality calibration sessions, AI-aware promotion path for agents. From "AI = a tool" — to "AI = part of how we operate".
cs-team-workflow.why: Individual AI usage in support does not work — consistency for customers is needed (everyone gets same quality answer). Team workflow ensures this through shared setup + processes.
cs-team-workflow.when: When team ≥5 agents use AI. When new agents arrive and "do not know how". When quality is inconsistent between shift teams.
cs-team-workflow.impact: Team velocity: agents process 50%+ more tickets. New agent onboarding: from 4 weeks to 2 weeks. Quality consistency across shifts: +60%. AI literacy team-wide.
cs-team-workflow.example:
CS Team Setup:

1. Shared Claude Project "Support Workspace":
   - KB indexed
   - Brand voice guide (tone for customers)
   - Common scenarios templates

2. [[node:cc-md|CLAUDE.md]]: response guidelines, escalation criteria, tone rules.

3. Skills: response-drafter, ticket-summarizer, escalation-formatter.

4. Weekly calibration: team reviews 5 AI-handled tickets together. Discusses: what worked, what would change.

5. AI-aware promotion: agents who improve AI workflow get senior path (not just "answer more tickets").

Result: team functions as a cohesive AI-augmented unit.
cs-team-workflow.mistakes: Treating AI usage as "individual perk". Without team-level workflow, customers get inconsistent experience (depending on which agent picks). AI = team capability, not individual skill.

uc-ai-support-tier1.title: Launch AI Tier-1 Support
uc-ai-support-tier1.what: Full path from "all by hand" to "AI closes 40% of tickets". Cross-layer path through 7 nodes: Foundation, then [[node:ai-fundamentals|AI Fundamentals]], then Systems, then Transformation.
uc-ai-support-tier1.why: Tier-1 automation = highest-ROI AI project in support. This UC shows a structured approach (not "buy a bot"): KB first, then AI, then quality monitoring.
uc-ai-support-tier1.when: Tier-1 volume >100 tickets/week. Baseline CSAT exists for comparison. Can invest 3-4 weeks in setup. Buy-in from CS-lead AND product (for KB).
uc-ai-support-tier1.impact: Outcome: working tier-1 AI with 40% deflection in 4 weeks. Metrics: deflection rate from 0 to 40%, median response time from 4h to 2min for AI-tickets, CSAT maintained at baseline.
uc-ai-support-tier1.example:
Path (7 steps):

Week 1: Knowledge Base prep.
1. Foundation: af-rag-basics, understand what RAG needs
2. Foundation: af-vector-db, vector DB choice (pgvector usually enough)
3. Systems: sys-rag-architecture, pattern choice (Advanced RAG mandatory)
4. Audit + restructure existing KB articles

Week 2: AI tier-1 setup.
5. Foundation: prompting, [[node:b-system|system prompt]] for support bot
6. Foundation: projects, create "Support Bot" Project with KB
7. Transformation: cs-tier1, build workflow with quality gates

Week 3: Quality + escalation.
8. Transformation: cs-escalation, correct routing for escalations
9. Transformation: cs-quality-monitoring, setup random sample review

Week 4: Roll-out.
10. Pilot on 1 ticket category. Measure deflection + CSAT.
11. Expand to 3-5 categories. Iterate.

Stage transition: from stage 1 to stage 2.
uc-ai-support-tier1.mistakes: Launching AI tier-1 without KB ops first. If the KB is not suitable for AI retrieval (bad structure, outdated) — AI will answer generic or wrong. KB ops = 50% of UC work. Do not skip.

pd-discovery-research.title: AI Discovery Research
pd-discovery-research.what: AI-powered user research: automatic interview synthesis, competitive analysis, market research. From "read 20 interviews in 3 days" — to "AI extracts themes in an hour, PM validates".
pd-discovery-research.why: Discovery is the most time-intensive part of PM work. 50 interviews = a week of manual synthesis. AI does a first pass in an hour, the PM focuses on validation and interpretation.
pd-discovery-research.when: When there are >10 interviews/customer calls on one topic. When quarterly customer research is needed. When the competitive landscape changes and you need to track it.
pd-discovery-research.impact: Time-to-insight: from days to hours. Coverage: PM can "process" 50 interviews instead of 10. Quality: structured themes instead of "here are my notes".
pd-discovery-research.example:
Research Synthesis Workflow:

  Inputs:
  - 30 interview transcripts
  - Customer support tickets (1 month)
  - Competitor reviews on G2/Trustpilot
        ↓
  Project "Research" with RAG index
        ↓
  AI Steps:
  1. Extract themes (frequency + sentiment)
  2. Cluster similar quotes
  3. Identify gaps (what people often mention but we do not do)
  4. Generate hypothesis matrix
        ↓
  PM validates: which themes are actionable, which need follow-up
        ↓
  Output: structured research report + raw data accessible

Metric: time-to-insight, theme coverage.
pd-discovery-research.mistakes: Relying on AI without human validation. AI misses nuance: irony, edge cases, cultural context. Workflow: AI extracts, then PM validates a 10-20% sample, then confidence in the rest grows. Without validation — false insights.

pd-spec-generation.title: AI Spec Generation
pd-spec-generation.what: AI writes PRDs, user stories, technical specs from a rough idea + research input. From "PM sits for 2 days writing a PRD" — to "PM iterates with AI for 2 hours, draft is ready".
pd-spec-generation.why: PRD writing is a shipping bottleneck. PMs spend days formatting/structuring what they already know in their heads. AI handles the "writing" part, the PM focuses on content quality.
pd-spec-generation.when: When the team loses momentum between "have an idea" and "PRD written". When there is a documented PRD template. When rough notes / research are already on hand.
pd-spec-generation.impact: Time-to-PRD: from 2 days to 4 hours (including iterations). Consistency: a single format for all specs. Quality: AI catches missing sections (success metrics, edge cases, etc.).
pd-spec-generation.example:
Spec Generation Workflow:

  Input for AI:
  - Rough idea (3-5 sentences from PM)
  - Research output (from pd-discovery)
  - Existing PRD template + 2-3 high-quality examples
        ↓
  AI generates:
  - Problem statement
  - User stories with acceptance criteria
  - Success metrics proposals
  - Open questions
  - Technical considerations (for engineering)
        ↓
  PM iterates: 3-5 rounds of edits
        ↓
  Output: ship-ready PRD

Metric: time-to-spec, dev team feedback on PRD quality.
pd-spec-generation.mistakes: Doing AI-PRDs without research input. "Write a PRD for feature X" = generic stuff. Quality output requires quality input: research, examples, constraints. Garbage in = garbage out.

pd-roadmap-intelligence.title: AI Roadmap Intelligence
pd-roadmap-intelligence.what: AI helps with roadmap prioritization: analyzing feedback patterns, competitor moves, customer requests, internal data, then ranked priorities with reasoning. AI = "second analyst" in roadmap discussions.
pd-roadmap-intelligence.why: Roadmap prioritization is usually done "by gut" under stakeholder pressure. AI brings a structured framework: explicit weights, data-based scoring, consideration of alternatives.
pd-roadmap-intelligence.when: Quarterly planning. Before a roadmap review with executives. When "everyone has their own opinion" and a structured framework is needed for the decision.
pd-roadmap-intelligence.impact: Reactive prioritization: -60%. Stakeholder alignment: faster (data, not opinions). Roadmap thrashing: reduced (explicit criteria prevent frequent changes).
pd-roadmap-intelligence.example:
Roadmap Prioritization Workflow:

  Inputs:
  - All product opportunities (backlog + new ideas)
  - Customer feedback themes (from feedback-synthesis)
  - Competitor analysis
  - Internal metrics (revenue impact, retention)
  - Strategic objectives (current quarter)
        ↓
  AI Scoring:
  - Each opportunity rated on: impact, effort, strategic fit, risk
  - Reasoning explicit for each
  - Alternative orderings played out
        ↓
  PM + leadership: review AI ranking + override based on judgment
        ↓
  Output: prioritized roadmap with documented reasoning

Value: next quarter you CAN explain "why we chose this".
pd-roadmap-intelligence.mistakes: Accepting AI roadmap as final. AI scoring is based on the data you gave — but it does not know board politics, executive priorities, or upcoming launches. AI = input into a decision, not the decision itself.

pd-experimentation.title: AI Feature Experimentation
pd-experimentation.what: AI support for A/B testing: hypothesis generation, variant design, statistical analysis interpretation, learnings synthesis. From "ran A/B, forgot results" — to "structured experimentation engine".
pd-experimentation.why: Most teams run A/B tests poorly: weak hypotheses, no power analysis, results forgotten. AI structures this: forces explicit hypothesis, generates variant ideas, helps interpret results.
pd-experimentation.when: When the team runs ≥3 experiments per quarter. When experiment outputs do not turn into product knowledge. When you need to scale experimentation across multiple teams.
pd-experimentation.impact: Experiment velocity: +50%. Experiments with clear learnings: from 50% to 90%. Knowledge retention: structured library of experiment outcomes.
pd-experimentation.example:
Experimentation Workflow:

  1. Hypothesis Generation:
     - PM inputs: "hypothesis: shorter onboarding, higher activation"
     - AI critiques: "specify metric, magnitude, timeframe, sample needed"
     - Result: "If we cut onboarding from 5 to 2 steps, activation rate +15% over 4 weeks (n>1000)"

  2. Variant Design:
     - AI generates 3-5 specific variant approaches
     - Discusses pros/cons of each

  3. Post-experiment Analysis:
     - Input: results data
     - AI: "winner with X confidence. Caveats: ... Recommended follow-up: ..."

  4. Library:
     - AI maintains experiment knowledge base
     - Search: "did we try X before?"

Metric: experiments per quarter, learnings library size.
pd-experimentation.mistakes: Using AI for "predict before run". AI cannot predict the result of an A/B (if it could — an A/B would not be needed). AI is good at: hypothesis sharpening, variant ideation, post-analysis interpretation. Not predictive.

pd-feedback-synthesis.title: AI Feedback Synthesis
pd-feedback-synthesis.what: AI reads all user feedback (NPS comments, support tickets, reviews, sales notes), then structured insights with trends. From "PM read ~50 comments" — to "AI processed 5000 and found patterns".
pd-feedback-synthesis.why: Customer feedback is fragmented across 5-10 sources. The PM physically cannot read everything. AI does aggregation + synthesis. Sentiment shifts visible before they show up in churn.
pd-feedback-synthesis.when: When there are ≥3 feedback sources (NPS, support, reviews, sales calls, social). When the product team wants "voice of customer" systematic, not anecdotal.
pd-feedback-synthesis.impact: Coverage: 5% of feedback is read, then 100% is processed. Time-to-trend: from 2 months to 2 weeks. Decision quality: data-backed instead of "I remember someone complained".
pd-feedback-synthesis.example:
**Feedback synthesis pipeline:**

**1. Sources (weekly):**
- NPS responses (quarterly × 1000+)
- Support tickets with CSAT comments
- App Store / G2 reviews
- Sales call notes
- Social mentions

**2. AI processing:**
- Clean + dedupe
- Categorize (feature, UX, pricing, performance, ...)
- Sentiment analysis
- Theme extraction
- Trend detection (week-over-week)

**3. Weekly output:**
- Top 5 themes (with magnitude + delta)
- Quote samples for each
- Critical issues to investigate

**4. Distribution:**
- Product team, then decisions
- Engineering, then bug themes
- Marketing, then positioning themes

**Metrics:** feedback coverage, time-to-action on trending issues.
pd-feedback-synthesis.mistakes: Doing feedback synthesis in a vacuum. Output must flow into roadmap planning, not into a read-only report. Workflow: synthesis, then product review, then roadmap update, then measure impact. Without the loop — polite theater.

pd-product-analytics.title: AI Product Analytics
pd-product-analytics.what: AI reads product usage data (Amplitude, Mixpanel, GA), then writes insight reports with hypotheses "why did this happen?" and suggested investigations. From "here is a dashboard" — to "here is what happened and what it means".
pd-product-analytics.why: Product analytics tools show "what happened", but not "why". PM/analytics manager spends hours on formulating hypotheses. AI does this first-pass, the human verifies.
pd-product-analytics.when: Weekly product reviews. After every major release. When a metric is unexpected (growth or drop). When the team "does not understand why" something is happening.
pd-product-analytics.impact: Time-to-hypothesis: from days to hours. Coverage: analytics-aware decisions grow from 30% to 70%+ of the team.
pd-product-analytics.example:
Weekly Product Analytics Workflow:

  Inputs:
  - Top-line metrics (DAU, MAU, retention, activation)
  - Feature usage (new + existing)
  - User segments behavior
  - Recent product releases
        ↓
  AI Analysis:
  1. What changed (numbers + delta + significance)
  2. Correlation: "release X, metric Y +Z%"
  3. Anomaly detection (unusual segment behavior)
  4. Hypotheses (ranked by likelihood)
  5. Recommended investigations (queries to run, segments to look at)
        ↓
  Product team:
  - Validates top hypotheses
  - Decides actions
  - Adds learnings to knowledge base

Metric: % of metric changes with documented explanation.
pd-product-analytics.mistakes: Trusting AI causal claims. "Release X caused metric Y +5%" — that is correlation, not causation. AI recommends a hypothesis, the human must validate via proper analysis (cohort, A/B, before-after).

pd-team-workflow.title: AI Product Team Workflow
pd-team-workflow.what: Product team operating model with AI: shared research workspace, common spec templates, feedback synthesis pipeline, weekly AI office hours. From "every PM with their own Claude" — to a "collaborative AI-powered product team".
pd-team-workflow.why: Individual usage in product does not scale — research findings are lost between PMs, specs are inconsistent, knowledge is not shared. Team workflow creates a shared institutional memory.
pd-team-workflow.when: Product team ≥3 PMs use AI. When "everyone has their own approach to specs". When research findings are lost after launch. When a new PM "does not know how we work".
pd-team-workflow.impact: Team velocity: +30%. New PM onboarding: from 6 weeks to 3 weeks (via shared knowledge). Decision quality: improves over time (institutional memory grows).
pd-team-workflow.example:
Product Team Setup:

1. Shared Claude Project "Product Workspace":
   - All research transcripts indexed
   - Past PRDs library
   - Experiment learnings
   - Customer feedback (categorized)

2. [[node:cc-md|CLAUDE.md]]: writing conventions, PRD template, decision frameworks.

3. Skills:
   - research-synthesizer
   - prd-drafter
   - feedback-categorizer
   - experiment-designer

4. Weekly "AI office hours" 30 min:
   - Best prompt discoveries
   - Failed AI experiments (what is not working)
   - Cross-team learning

5. Quarterly knowledge curation:
   - What to add to shared workspace
   - What is outdated and to remove

Stage 3 sign: new PM writes a shipping-ready PRD by the end of the first month.
pd-team-workflow.mistakes: Doing team workflow without a librarian role. Shared workspace without maintainership = junk drawer in 6 months. Someone must curate: weekly review of new content, monthly cleanup of outdated.

uc-ai-discovery-launch.what: Full path from "doing research by hand" to "AI-powered discovery pipeline". Cross-layer path through 6 nodes: Foundation, then Systems, then Transformation.
uc-ai-discovery-launch.why: The most common product team request: "we have tons of interviews / feedback / research, but synthesis is a bottleneck". This UC solves it systematically via RAG + workflows + product practices.
uc-ai-discovery-launch.when: When the product team has ≥30 interviews or ≥100 feedback items without structured processing. When the discovery, then ship cycle is slow. When there is buy-in from Head of Product.
uc-ai-discovery-launch.impact: Outcome: working AI-discovery pipeline in 2 weeks. Metrics: time-to-insight ≤2 hours per topic, research coverage 100% (vs 30% manually), structured theme extraction.
uc-ai-discovery-launch.example:

uc-ai-discovery-launch.mistakes: Doing a UC without structured research input. If interviews are scattered chaotically across Notion / Google Docs / Slack — AI cannot find them. Day 1 work = organize the research repository. This is 30% of UC time. Do not skip.

uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.title: Enterprise AI Transformation Roadmap
uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.what: Full path from "doing AI pilots ad-hoc" to "AI-native company-wide operations". Cross-layer + cross-direction path: enterprise strategy, then tactical roll-outs, then org-wide change. 6-12 months of work.
uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.why: This is the highest-level UC in 105 Atlas — for CEO/CIO/Head of AI. Shows how a company systematically does AI transformation across ALL departments at once with governance + measurement.
uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.when: When the company commits to AI transformation strategically (not isolated pilots). When there is executive buy-in. When there is resource commitment ($M+ budget) for 12-24 months.
uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.impact: Outcome: company at Stage 3 AI-native operations in 12 months. Metrics: 4+ tactical directions running, $X ROI documented, governance in place, 80%+ team AI-proficient.
uc-ai-transformation-roadmap.example:
Roadmap (12 months):
